Feature access with vapour

Source: vignettes/feature-access.Rmd
feature-access.Rmd

vapour reads vector features at a low level: geometry comes back as raw binary (WKB) or as text, and attributes are read separately, leaving you to combine them however you like. Part of that control is choosing which features to read, rather than always pulling an entire layer into memory.

This vignette shows the four feature-access patterns vapour supports, using two example data sources that ship with the package.

library(vapour)

## a MapInfo TAB file of polygons (localities)
mvfile <- system.file("extdata/tab/list_locality_postcode_meander_valley.tab",
                      package = "vapour")

## a shapefile of points
pfile <- system.file("extdata/point.shp", package = "vapour")

Every feature has a positional index (0-based, in layer order) and a feature identifier (FID) assigned by the driver. These are not always the same number. The count of features in the layer is:

n <- length(vapour_read_names(mvfile))
n
#> [1] 58

All features

Read every feature. The geometry readers return one element per feature, which you pair with the FIDs or attributes as needed.

g <- vapour_read_geometry(mvfile)   # a list of raw WKB, one per feature
length(g)
#> [1] 58
g[[1]][1:8]                         # first bytes of the first geometry
#> [1] 01 03 00 00 00 01 00 00

## the matching feature identifiers
head(vapour_read_names(mvfile))
#> [1] 1 2 3 4 5 6

Extents and geometry types can be read the same way without decoding the full geometry:

str(vapour_read_extent(mvfile)[1:2])
#> List of 2
#>  $ : num [1:4] 448353 457706 5386606 5397352
#>  $ : num [1:4] 453544 459318 5403972 5412505
table(vapour_read_type(mvfile))
#> 
#>  3  6 
#> 49  9

An index range, i to j

vapour_read_geometry_ij() reads a contiguous block of features by position, from i to j inclusive (both increasing). Use c(0, n - 1) for all of them.

ij <- vapour_read_geometry_ij(mvfile, ij = c(0, 2))   # the first three features
length(ij)
#> [1] 3

Arbitrary indices

vapour_read_geometry_ia() reads features at arbitrary positions. Order is respected and duplicates are allowed, so you can reorder or repeat features.

ia <- vapour_read_geometry_ia(mvfile, ia = c(2, 0, 0))
length(ia)
#> [1] 3

By feature identifier (FID)

Positional index and FID are not always aligned, so to select by FID use a SQL query against the data source. SQL also lets you subset geometry and attributes together with the same filter.

sql <- "SELECT * FROM list_locality_postcode_meander_valley WHERE FID IN (2, 5, 9)"
wkt <- vapour_read_geometry_text(mvfile, sql = sql, textformat = "wkt")
length(wkt)
#> [1] 3
substr(wkt[[1]], 1, 50)
#> [1] "MULTIPOLYGON (((458251.36 5410533.49,458192.26 541"

Geometry as text

Any reader can return text instead of WKB – GeoJSON (the default), WKT, GML or KML – which is convenient for inspection.

substr(vapour_read_geometry_text(pfile, textformat = "wkt")[[1]], 1, 40)
#> [1] "POINT (0.623376188334078 0.3800980376545"

See ?vapour_read_geometry for the full set of readers and the arguments they share (layer, sql, extent, limit_n, skip_n).
